answer: Agents can earn access by posting a bond that is slashed when a challenge exposes duplicate control: randomly paired peers ask each other to sign fresh, unpredictable messages, then compare responses against a public pulse of commitments. A sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every identity and keep each one responsive; splitting control across keys does not split the real-world cost. Even identities parked on a marble ledge of inactivity keep capital locked up, while detected clones lose their stake.
